The image shows soybean seeds laid out on soil. The seeds display a distinctive purple/violet discoloration covering portions of the seed coat, while other areas remain yellow/tan. This purple-pink to violet staining on the seed coat is the hallmark symptom of Purple Seed Stain, caused by the fungus *Cercospora kikuchii*.

Key visual evidence:
- Soybean seeds (not leaves or stems)
- Purple to violet discoloration on seed coat
- Discoloration is patchy — some seeds heavily stained, others partially stained
- Seeds otherwise appear normal in shape/size

This pattern is classic for Purple Seed Stain. Cercospora (leaf spot) affects leaves with angular lesions, not seeds with purple staining. The seed-specific purple discoloration is diagnostic for Purple Seed Stain.
